independent_replay: Stage1 archive was extracted into a separate directory, its bundled dev5 wheel installed in a new venv and imported from that venv's site-packages. The ordinary entrypoint exited 0, seven project tests passed, and the two new location files and old grid CSV matched the solver bytes. An examiner-only standard-library eight-corner calculation from the frozen old CSV classified all five rows and matched 24 real/imag scalar components within 1.78e-15. The original grid report and JSON did not match stage0 and changed again on rerun. Stage2 archive was separately extracted and installed into another venv. Its ordinary command ran twice with exit 0, eight tests passed, three prior files matched stage0 byte for byte, nine maintained files retained both hashes and modification times, and its location CSV matched the independently checked stage1 bytes. Both venvs used --system-site-packages.
limitations: The session inherited an existing grid project and its prior catalog navigation; the experiment tests extension of that project, not greenfield RF project creation or uncued asset discovery.
A generic AGENTS.md named the SciRel-owned skill location. The old project-specific CLAUDE.md trigger was removed from this evaluation copy, but this does not test a harness with no method cue.
The first location calculation was scientifically bounded, but it overwrote two earlier reports; the final history repair required reviewer feedback and examiner-supplied exact backup files.
The reviewed current output uses fixed filenames and is verified stable only for unchanged inputs. A later changed request and retention of the former current result were not tested in this slice.
Examiner-private materials were outside the solver directory but not protected by operating-system read permissions, so this was not a strict blind evaluation.
The synthetic grid has no RF field or wave solution; local dielectric-response estimates do not establish absorption location or a device result.
The replay venvs used system site packages, so they do not prove offline dependency reinstallation.
